phase1.intro:
So far, the storefront has only spoken through what's permanently on screen. Alert is the "may I help you?" moment.

Where should we start?

topics.buttonText: What's the difference between show() and showAndWait()?
dialogue: `new Alert(Alert.AlertType.CONFIRMATION, "Are you sure?")` builds a dialog; `showAndWait()` [[key:blocks — your code pauses right there until the user closes the dialog]], unlike `show()`, which returns immediately. For a yes/no decision, you almost always want showAndWait().

stickyNote.flavor: ⏸️ showAndWait() pauses your code until closed
stickyNote.definition: show() displays a dialog and returns immediately. showAndWait() blocks execution until the user closes it — needed when you need their answer.

topics.buttonText: How do I check which button the user picked?
dialogue: AlertType comes in a few built-in flavors — INFORMATION, WARNING, ERROR, CONFIRMATION — each with its own default icon and buttons. showAndWait() returns an Optional<ButtonType>, and checking `result.get() == ButtonType.OK` (after `.isPresent()`) is how you branch on what the user picked.

stickyNote.flavor: 🔘 an Optional<ButtonType> tells you the choice
stickyNote.definition: AlertType (INFORMATION/WARNING/ERROR/CONFIRMATION) sets default icon/buttons. showAndWait() returns Optional<ButtonType> to check the user's choice.

topics.buttonText: What happens if I forget to call show() on an Alert?
dialogue: [[warn:Building an Alert without calling show() or showAndWait() does nothing]] — the same failure pattern as a Stage you never called show() on back in 5.2. A fully configured Alert sitting in memory is invisible until one of those calls actually displays it.

stickyNote.flavor: 👻 configured but invisible without a display call
stickyNote.definition: A fully built Alert object does nothing until show() or showAndWait() is called — same pattern as a Stage without show().

phase1.output: (Window with buttons that open various types of dialogs and alerts)
phase1.openingDialogue: Alert pops up a conversation — showAndWait() blocks for an answer, and nothing shows without calling one of the display methods. 🔘

phase2.errorMessage: (Window appears but the alert is NEVER SHOWN!)
phase2.explanation:
[[warn:the button click runs, nothing crashes, and the alert simply never shows up]].

An Alert was constructed with a title and a message — every configuration step is correct — but [[key:the code stops one call short]]: neither show() nor showAndWait() was ever invoked. Same lesson as a Stage that's built but never shown: JavaFX never displays anything on its own initiative, no matter how completely you've configured it. Every window, every dialog, needs its own explicit "now actually put this on screen" call.

mcq.question:
You call alert.show() (not showAndWait()) right before a line that immediately hides the main window. What actually happens?

A) The alert blocks until closed, exactly like showAndWait()
B) The next line runs immediately without waiting — show() doesn't pause execution
C) A compile error, since show() requires a return value to be captured
D) The alert never appears because show() is asynchronous and gets cancelled

phase4.selfChallenge:
Write a program that:
1. Has a Button "Delete File"
2. When clicked, shows a CONFIRMATION alert with message "Are you sure you want to delete this file?"
3. If OK is clicked, prints "File deleted!" to a Label
4. If Cancel is clicked, prints "Deletion cancelled" to a Label

phase5.trivia: [[fun:showAndWait() can't be called from a background thread]] — like every other JavaFX UI operation, it has to run on the JavaFX Application Thread, so a long-running task can't just pop up its own "are you sure" dialog mid-calculation without first handing control back to the UI thread.
